WITH mol_cl AS (

questions.nlq: Please list the molecule_id and its carcinogenic label for each molecule that contains many chlorine atoms, together with the total number of atoms in that molecule, and order the results by the percentage of chlorine atoms descending.

meanings.hidden_knowledge: In this context, the term 'many' means that the molecule has at least five (5) chlorine atoms.
meanings.gt_sql:
SELECT a.molecule_id,
       m.label,
       COUNT(*) AS total_atoms
FROM atom a
JOIN molecule m ON a.molecule_id = m.molecule_id
GROUP BY a.molecule_id
HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN a.element = 'cl' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) >= 5
ORDER BY (SUM(CASE WHEN a.element = 'cl' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 1.0) / COUNT(*) DESC;

meanings.hidden_knowledge: In this context, the term 'many' means that the molecule has at least ten (10) chlorine atoms.

SELECT molecule_id, label, total_atoms
FROM (
    SELECT a.molecule_id,
           m.label,
           COUNT(*) AS total_atoms,
           SUM(CASE WHEN a.element = 'cl' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS chlorine_cnt
    FROM atom a
    JOIN molecule m ON a.molecule_id = m.molecule_id
    GROUP BY a.molecule_id
    HAVING chlorine_cnt >= 10
) sub
ORDER BY (chlorine_cnt * 1.0 / total_atoms) DESC;

questions.nlq: I would like to identify the molecule identifiers for all carcinogenic compounds that contain a substantially long continuous chain of carbon atoms connected by single bonds.

meanings.hidden_knowledge: The term substantially long specifies a minimum threshold of 10 consecutive carbon atoms linked by single bonds within the molecule structure.
meanings.gt_sql:
WITH RECURSIVE 
carbon_atoms AS (
    SELECT atom_id, molecule_id 
    FROM atom 
    WHERE element = 'c'
),

chain_search AS (
    SELECT 
        a1.atom_id AS start_atom,
        a1.atom_id AS current_atom,
        a1.molecule_id,
        1 AS chain_length,
        '|' || a1.atom_id || '|' AS visited
    FROM carbon_atoms a1
    
    UNION ALL
    
    SELECT 
        cs.start_atom,
        c2.atom_id AS current_atom,
        cs.molecule_id,
        cs.chain_length + 1 AS chain_length,
        cs.visited || c2.atom_id || '|' AS visited
    FROM chain_search cs
    JOIN atom a1 ON a1.atom_id = cs.current_atom
    JOIN connected conn ON a1.atom_id = conn.atom_id OR a1.atom_id = conn.atom_id2
    JOIN atom a2 ON (a2.atom_id = conn.atom_id2 AND a1.atom_id != a2.atom_id) OR (a2.atom_id = conn.atom_id AND a1.atom_id != a2.atom_id)
    JOIN bond b ON conn.bond_id = b.bond_id
    JOIN carbon_atoms c2 ON c2.atom_id = a2.atom_id
    WHERE a1.molecule_id = a2.molecule_id
      AND b.bond_type = '-'
      AND cs.visited NOT LIKE '%|' || c2.atom_id || '|%'
      AND cs.chain_length < 20
)

SELECT DISTINCT cs.molecule_id
FROM chain_search cs
JOIN molecule m ON cs.molecule_id = m.molecule_id
WHERE cs.chain_length >= 10
  AND m.label = '+'

    JOIN atom a2 ON c.atom_id2 = a2.atom_id

questions.nlq: Retrieve the identifiers of molecules that contain many atoms reachable from a nitrogen atom via a path of at most three bonds.

meanings.hidden_knowledge: The term many means more than 10 reachable atoms per molecule.
meanings.gt_sql:
WITH RECURSIVE
    nitrogen AS (
        SELECT atom_id, molecule_id
        FROM atom
        WHERE element = 'n'
    ),
    reach AS (
        SELECT n.atom_id AS start_atom, n.atom_id AS current_atom, 0 AS depth, n.molecule_id
        FROM nitrogen n
        UNION ALL
        SELECT r.start_atom,
               CASE
                   WHEN c.atom_id = r.current_atom THEN c.atom_id2
                   ELSE c.atom_id
               END AS current_atom,
               r.depth + 1,
               r.molecule_id
        FROM reach r
        JOIN connected c ON (c.atom_id = r.current_atom OR c.atom_id2 = r.current_atom)
        JOIN atom a2 ON (CASE WHEN c.atom_id = r.current_atom THEN c.atom_id2 ELSE c.atom_id END) = a2.atom_id
                       AND a2.molecule_id = r.molecule_id
        WHERE r.depth < 3
    )
    SELECT DISTINCT molecule_id
    FROM (
        SELECT start_atom, molecule_id, COUNT(DISTINCT current_atom) AS reachable_cnt
        FROM reach
        GROUP BY start_atom, molecule_id
        HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT current_atom) > 10
    ) sub;

        SELECT atom_id, molecule_id
        FROM atom

        SELECT n.atom_id AS start, a.atom_id AS atom, 0 AS d
        FROM nitrogen n
        JOIN atom a ON a.atom_id = n.atom_id
        UNION ALL
        SELECT r.start, a2.atom_id, r.d + 1
        FROM reach r
        JOIN connected c ON c.atom_id = r.atom
        JOIN atom a2 ON a2.atom_id = c.atom_id2
        WHERE r.d < 3

            FROM reach
            GROUP BY start
        ) rc ON rc.start = n.atom_id
        WHERE n.molecule_id = m.molecule_id

SELECT a.molecule_id
FROM atom a
WHERE a.element = 'cl'
GROUP BY a.molecule_id
HAVING COUNT(*) > 3;
SELECT a.molecule_id FROM atom a WHERE a.element = 'cl' GROUP BY a.molecule_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 3
SELECT molecule_id FROM atom WHERE element='cl' GROUP BY molecule_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 3;

SELECT m.molecule_id
FROM molecule m
LEFT JOIN atom a ON a.molecule_id = m.molecule_id AND a.element = 'cl'
GROUP BY m.molecule_id
HAVING COUNT(a.atom_id) > (
    SELECT AVG(cl_count)
    FROM (
        SELECT m2.molecule_id, COUNT(a2.atom_id) AS cl_count
        FROM molecule m2
        LEFT JOIN atom a2 ON a2.molecule_id = m2.molecule_id AND a2.element = 'cl'
        GROUP BY m2.molecule_id
    ) AS sub
);

WITH all_molecules AS (
    SELECT molecule_id FROM molecule
),
chlorine_counts AS (
    SELECT 
        am.molecule_id,
        COUNT(a.atom_id) AS cl_count
    FROM all_molecules am
    LEFT JOIN atom a ON am.molecule_id = a.molecule_id AND a.element = 'cl'
    GROUP BY am.molecule_id
),
average_cl AS (
    SELECT AVG(cl_count) AS avg_count
    FROM chlorine_counts
)
SELECT mc.molecule_id
FROM chlorine_counts mc, average_cl ac
WHERE mc.cl_count > ac.avg_count

SELECT molecule_id FROM (SELECT a.molecule_id, SUM(CASE WHEN a.element='cl' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS chlorine_count FROM atom a GROUP BY a.molecule_id) t WHERE t.chlorine_count > (SELECT (SUM(CASE WHEN element='cl' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 1.0) / COUNT(DISTINCT molecule_id) FROM atom);

WITH atom_stats AS (
    SELECT 
        molecule_id,
        SUM(CASE WHEN element = 'cl' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS cl_count,
        COUNT(*) AS total_count
    FROM atom
    GROUP BY molecule_id
)
SELECT molecule_id, cl_count
FROM atom_stats
WHERE cl_count * 1.0 / total_count > 0.30

WITH counts AS (
    SELECT a.molecule_id,
           COUNT(*) AS total_atoms,
           SUM(CASE WHEN a.element = 'cl' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS chlorine_count
    FROM atom a
    GROUP BY a.molecule_id
)
SELECT c.molecule_id,
       c.chlorine_count
FROM counts c
WHERE c.chlorine_count > 0.3 * c.total_atoms;

SELECT b.molecule_id
FROM bond AS b
GROUP BY b.molecule_id
HAVING COUNT(*) > 10;
SELECT m.molecule_id FROM molecule m JOIN bond b ON m.molecule_id = b.molecule_id GROUP BY m.molecule_id HAVING COUNT(b.bond_id) > 10

SELECT m.molecule_id
FROM molecule m
JOIN (
    SELECT b.molecule_id, COUNT(*) AS bond_count
    FROM bond b
    GROUP BY b.molecule_id
) b_cnt ON m.molecule_id = b_cnt.molecule_id
WHERE b_cnt.bond_count > 10;

WITH bond_counts AS (
    SELECT molecule_id, COUNT(*) AS bond_cnt
    FROM bond
    GROUP BY molecule_id
),
avg_cnt AS (
    SELECT AVG(bond_cnt) AS avg_bond_cnt
    FROM bond_counts
)
SELECT bc.molecule_id
FROM bond_counts bc, avg_cnt
WHERE bc.bond_cnt > avg_cnt.avg_bond_cnt;
SELECT b.molecule_id FROM bond b GROUP BY b.molecule_id HAVING COUNT(*) > (SELECT AVG(bond_count) FROM (SELECT molecule_id, COUNT(*) AS bond_count FROM bond GROUP BY molecule_id))

WITH mol_bond_count AS (
    SELECT m.molecule_id, COUNT(b.bond_id) AS bond_count
    FROM molecule m
    LEFT JOIN bond b ON m.molecule_id = b.molecule_id
    GROUP BY m.molecule_id
),
avg_bonds AS (
    SELECT AVG(bond_count) AS avg_bond_count
    FROM mol_bond_count
)
SELECT mbc.molecule_id
FROM mol_bond_count mbc, avg_bonds ab
WHERE mbc.bond_count > ab.avg_bond_count;

questions.nlq: Hey! Could you help me pull up all the molecules that have a lot of chlorine atoms? I'd love to see their molecule_id, the total number of atoms, how many chlorine atoms they contain, and whether they're carcinogenic.

meanings.gt_sql:
SELECT a.molecule_id,
       COUNT(*) AS total_atoms,
       SUM(CASE WHEN a.element = 'cl' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS chlorine_atoms,
       m.label
FROM atom AS a
JOIN molecule AS m ON a.molecule_id = m.molecule_id
GROUP BY a.molecule_id, m.label
HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN a.element = 'cl' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) >= 4;

meanings.hidden_knowledge: In this context, "a lot of chlorine atoms" means chlorine atoms make up **at least 35 % of all atoms in the molecule**.

  FROM ordered
  LIMIT 1
)

WHERE chl_cnt > (SELECT median FROM median_val);

questions.nlq: Could you tell me which molecules have a high number of chlorine atoms?

meanings.hidden_knowledge: The term *high* means the molecule contains **at least eight (8) chlorine atoms**.
meanings.gt_sql:
SELECT a.molecule_id
FROM atom AS a
WHERE a.element = 'cl'
GROUP BY a.molecule_id
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 8;

meanings.hidden_knowledge: The term *high* means the molecule's chlorine‑atom count falls within the **top 20 % of all molecules** when ranked by the number of chlorine atoms.
meanings.gt_sql:
WITH counts AS (
    SELECT m.molecule_id,
           COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN a.element = 'cl' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), 0) AS cl_count
    FROM molecule m
    LEFT JOIN atom a ON a.molecule_id = m.molecule_id
    GROUP BY m.molecule_id
),
ranked AS (
    SELECT molecule_id,
           cl_count,
           NTILE(5) OVER (ORDER BY cl_count DESC) AS quintile
    FROM counts
)
SELECT molecule_id
FROM ranked
WHERE quintile = 1;

SELECT a.molecule_id
FROM atom AS a
WHERE a.element = 'cl'
GROUP BY a.molecule_id
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 4;
SELECT molecule_id FROM atom WHERE element = 'cl' GROUP BY molecule_id HAVING COUNT(*) >= 4
SELECT "molecule_id" FROM "atom" WHERE "element" = 'cl' GROUP BY "molecule_id" HAVING COUNT(*) >= 4;

SELECT a.molecule_id
FROM (
    SELECT molecule_id,
           COUNT(*) AS total_atoms,
           SUM(CASE WHEN element = 'cl' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS cl_atoms
    FROM "atom"
    GROUP BY molecule_id
) a
WHERE cl_atoms * 1.0 / total_atoms >= 0.30;

SELECT a.molecule_id
FROM atom a
GROUP BY a.molecule_id
HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN a.element = 'cl' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(*) >= 30

WITH atom_counts AS (
        SELECT molecule_id,
               SUM(CASE WHEN element = 'c' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS carbon_cnt,
               COUNT(*) AS total_cnt,
               CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN element = 'c' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) / COUNT(*) AS ratio
        FROM atom
        GROUP BY molecule_id
    ),
    total AS (
        SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_mol FROM atom_counts
    ),
    ranked AS (
        SELECT ac.molecule_id,
               ac.ratio,
               ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY ac.ratio DESC) AS rn,
               t.total_mol
        FROM atom_counts ac
        CROSS JOIN total t
    )
SELECT molecule_id
FROM ranked
WHERE rn <= (total_mol + 9) / 10;

WITH atom_stats AS (
    SELECT 
        molecule_id,
        CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN element = 'c' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) / COUNT(*) as carbon_ratio
    FROM atom
    GROUP BY molecule_id
),
ranked AS (
    SELECT 
        molecule_id,
        carbon_ratio,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY carbon_ratio DESC) as row_num,
        COUNT(*) OVER () as total_count
    FROM atom_stats
)
SELECT molecule_id
FROM ranked
WHERE row_num <= ((total_count * 10 + 99) / 100)

WITH stable_mols AS (
    SELECT m.molecule_id
    FROM molecule m
    LEFT JOIN bond b ON b.molecule_id = m.molecule_id
    GROUP BY m.molecule_id
    HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN b.bond_type IS NULL OR b.bond_type <> '-' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) = 0
),
mol_ratios AS (
    SELECT sm.molecule_id,
           SUM(CASE WHEN a.element = 'c' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 1.0 / COUNT(*) AS carbon_ratio
    FROM stable_mols sm
    JOIN atom a ON a.molecule_id = sm.molecule_id
    GROUP BY sm.molecule_id
),
ranked AS (
    SELECT molecule_id,
           carbon_ratio,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY carbon_ratio DESC) AS rn,
           COUNT(*) OVER () AS total_mols
    FROM mol_ratios
)
SELECT molecule_id
FROM ranked
WHERE rn <= CEIL(0.1 * total_mols);

WITH bonds AS (

           b.molecule_id,
           b.bond_type,
           c.atom_id AS atom1,
           c.atom_id2 AS atom2
    FROM "bond" b
    JOIN "connected" c ON b.bond_id = c.bond_id
),
paths AS (
    SELECT b1.molecule_id,
           b1.atom1 AS start_atom,
           b1.atom2 AS mid1,
           b2.atom2 AS mid2,
           b3.atom2 AS end_atom
    FROM bonds b1
    JOIN bonds b2 ON b1.molecule_id = b2.molecule_id
                  AND b1.atom2 = b2.atom1
    JOIN bonds b3 ON b2.molecule_id = b3.molecule_id
                  AND b2.atom2 = b3.atom1
    WHERE b1.bond_type IN ('-','=')
      AND b2.bond_type IN ('-','=')
      AND b3.bond_type IN ('-','=')
      AND b1.bond_type != b2.bond_type
      AND b2.bond_type != b3.bond_type
)
SELECT molecule_id
FROM (
    SELECT molecule_id,
           COUNT(DISTINCT
               CASE WHEN start_atom < end_atom
                    THEN start_atom || '_' || mid1 || '_' || mid2 || '_' || end_atom
                    ELSE end_atom || '_' || mid2 || '_' || mid1 || '_' || start_atom
               END) AS chain_count
    FROM paths
    GROUP BY molecule_id
) WHERE chain_count >= 5;
